objective: Execute the full approved Kujo performance plan, preserving semantics and workloads; competitive performance must be measured, never presumed.
constraints: No Kostya contact or upstream submission
No changed algorithms, inputs, iterations, warmups or checksums
No benchmark-name special cases or benchmark-specific native kernels
No suppressed correctness checks; retain value semantics, errors, cancellation and capabilities
Experimental JIT remains opt-in until reliability and portability justify promotion
Unverified and timed-out cases remain visible; no extrapolated pass claims

stages.scope: Pin current builds and host conditions; sequential seven-sample VM/JIT/Goose/Rust comparisons, checksums, startup, total time and peak memory
CPU/allocation profiles and JIT execution/coverage/fallback evidence; reproducible cost and semantic test before optimization
Evidence-led calls, collections, numerics, strings, native boundaries and allocation fixes preserving language contracts
Audit and extend guarded JIT execution, fallback state, imports/captures/recursion where justified; measure startup; AOT only if evidence warrants
All 50 unchanged production VM checksums on candidate revision; separate interpreter and JIT evidence; no historical pass substitution
Both-runtime semantic tests, differential/generated JIT tests, deterministic cost/scaling checks and controlled performance CI; investigate repeatable >5% slowdowns
Per-case targets against faster comparator: within 2x, then 1.25x, then repeatable wins; report all failures, worst gaps, startup and memory without selective aggregates

Full relevant tests, Linux/macOS and supported-architecture gates, default-feature release artifacts, official local runner integration, concrete maintainer questions; no contact/submission without authorization

Fixed observed scalar VM arithmetic cases: errors now use existing handler unwind; nested calls, repeated failures, rethrow, compound-add atomicity and uncaught diagnostics pass both-runtime regressions. JIT failures remain separate and open.

Fixed reproduced callback failures: generated calls exit before later side effects, native ABI preserves original error, VM handlers unwind without replay. Nested calls and repeated failure/success reuse pass. Subsequent scalar global stores, Boolean results and checked native arithmetic fixes are tracked separately; general-value boundaries remain open. No speed claim.

Fixed reproduced Stack underflow in compiled caller to cold bytecode callee. Callback StoreVar/StoreLocal/StoreGlobal/DefineGlobal now peek and clone the assignment value, matching main VM; following Pop consumes it. Both new regressions fail before fix and pass after.

Fixed for tracked native scalar operands: arithmetic, ordering and unary guards reject invalid Boolean/integer operand kinds before native work and preserve canonical errors. Equality distinguishes scalar kinds; logical bytecodes normalize truthiness and return Bool. Existing global/loop-entry tagging and general-value gaps remain separate.

Fixed Boolean/integer named loads and whole-function scalar assignments. Load helpers publish scalar kind; regular/direct native lowering captures it. Explicit global loads bypass parameters and whole-function global stores preserve scalar types with checked assignment. Non-scalar globals and loop/script store paths remain separate. Direct native entrypoints now receive cached name metadata; shared table storage remains stable across cache growth. Regression tests require direct compilation and execution, including through a native wrapper.

Fixed reproduced verifier failure: branch edges carry paired payload/type arguments and establish destination stack depth for unconditional jumps and fallthroughs as well as conditional edges. All four compiler entrypoints restore typed stack joins; native compilation and direct recursion are tested. No timing claim.
Fixed reproduced VM ordering and logical-negation errors bypassing catch handlers. Those operations now use the existing result/error unwind path; interpreter, VM and JIT recovery tests pass.
Fixed in 8256219: callback Return/ReturnNone decrements recursion depth when removing the frame. Baseline sequential cold calls fail at call 256; regression covers 600 calls for each return opcode.

Partially resolved: Float and Null now use tagged immediate payloads through globals, scalar operators, assignments, callbacks, returns and loop-local persistence. Refreshed 15-run audit passes Int/Bool/Float/Null but still reproduces String returning Int(-1) in native code. String/object ownership and collection helper paths remain open; no general-value parity claim.

Fixed reproduced Float/Null global-return and implicit-return errors, plus loop float persistence as raw integer bits. Four-kind ABI preserves immediate types; native floating arithmetic, ordering, equality and truthiness retain VM contracts. Native function entry now accepts tagged immediate arguments; owned values remain guarded out. String/object paths remain open.

Confirmed coverage gap: compiler-generated ReleaseDeadLocal in copied-parameter loop prevents whole-function compilation. Copied loop remains correct via fallback in tests/jit_immediate_arguments.rs. Requires proper lifetime/slot semantics alongside native ownership work; do not count this fallback as native coverage.

Fixed confirmed bypass: pre-guard native Int400 and Float400.5 recursion returns successfully while reference runtimes reject depth256. Native entries now consume a budget shared with VM frames; direct recursion and callbacks release native slots on every generated normal/error exit. Separate active-native accounting survives VM error recovery. Bytecode call-entry errors now reach try/except. Tests include mutual native callbacks containing cold VM error recovery,300 caught deep failures followed by successful calls, and both-runtime/JIT depth limits.
